reviews.name: Obsession
reviews.reviewText:
Genuinely one of the best horror movies that's come out recently. It included a very well thought out horror arc and elements that kept my heart beating off my chest the whole time. There are some excellent narrative choices made in the story itself. Much that revolves around the cat, Sandy. Sandy getting to the pills were a gloomy start to the movie but also a great Chekhov's Gun. Also, the consistent misuse of Sandy's dead body, once in an almost ritualistic memorial, and then being literally fed to Bear adds a great metric to show the tell-tale signs of psychopathic behaviour in this altered 'Nikki'.
For a good amount of the film, Bear is genuinely scared and would (have) garnered my sympathy. I refuse to blame him for the initial wish because had it not been for the authenticity of the One Wish Willow's 'magic', it would've been an entirely personal prayer of frustration many of us could relate to. Many of us have wished that our crush would 'love us more than anyone else in the world'. That alone is not cruel, evil, or even slightly wrong. That is part of being hopeless.
And no, I will not blame him for not believing the sarcastic and dismissing-sounding 'disclaimer' by the staff at the till, or the fine print. Even Ian didn't believe it. I wouldn't, and you most probably wouldn't.
However, the issue lies in the fact that Bear's priority was to *alter* the wish and keep her despite knowing that she doesn't like him. His response to Nikki---desperate and in pain---asking him to 'please kill [her]' was 'What's so bad about being with me?' You don't need a reason to say no in these things. He is dick for that and he should be rightfully called out.
Nikki is evidently in pain and agony, and even takes momentary control of the body to try and escape this. It is horrifying to even attempt to imagine her experience of losing control of her body, being forced to be in a relationship with a guy she thinks of as a 'little brother', and go through all the horrid bits of eating cat food, peeing herself, killing Sarah and Ian---especially without the means to do more than a second of 'wtf?'. It is prominent that there are two intimate scenes shown where in one 'Nikki' snaps out and is horrified, and the other she really looks 'out of it'.
I also want to say that Bear was genuinely scared too. He spent much of the movie in a narrative that would've made me kms to make that stop much sooner. He is terrified and initially caves because 1) omggg my crush now suddenly likes me! 2) please leave me alone I'm scared you'd kill me and yourself if I try to leave. His later morbid obsession with saving a version of this where Nikki did not stare at him sleeping at night, and cook his dead cat, makes me lose sympathy (as mentioned above).
Special mentions go to Sarah. She was genuinely sweet and caring and had a generously built character in the movie. I really would've loved a world where she and Bear go together because they seemed so matching for each other, and the scene with her second-to-last letter back from college and them leaning on to each other made my heart melt. Sarah did not deserve to die---especially in such a painful, horrifying, and nightmare-inducing way. It was even heartbreaking to see that she did indeed get into Luther.
Overall, amazing movie, great plot, perfect scares, loved it, enjoyed it. Please don't make it about a gender war. Bear was horrible in ways that are un-absolvable, but he didn't intentionally start the horror of the story---no one did, except perhaps the people that sell the OWW.
PS Oh my God, how screwed up Nikki is now? She was seen as an unstable almost psychopathic individual by many people (at the restaurant, and Ian's 'Boys' Night Out') and now she is in a house with two murdered people and one who overdosed and killed themselves, whilst being drenched in cuts and blood herself. She is getting a couple consecutive lifetimes in prison, huh?
